facts.raw_span: A man in his late 60s presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule between the 3- and 6-o'clock positions
episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement
no visible iris seeding or aqueous cells
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy: Showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results: Showed monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation: Showed no other involvement
Staging: T2N0M0
Image A: Well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris lesion

concepts.why: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes support the diagnosis of primary iris lymphoma.

The biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes and the presence of few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes are consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule could also suggest iris melanoma, although the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.
The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement could suggest uveitis, although the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

The presence of ciliary body involvement on ultrasonographic biomicroscopy and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes could suggest choroidal lymphoma.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the absence of systemic involvement could suggest iris metastasis, although the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

The biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes and the presence of few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes are consistent with primary central nervous system lymphoma, although the clinical presentation does not support this diagnosis.

The presence of ciliary body involvement on ultrasonographic biomicroscopy and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes could suggest vitreoretinal lymphoma.

The absence of systemic involvement and the presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule could suggest systemic lymphoma with ocular involvement, although the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes could suggest ocular adnexal lymphoma.

rationales.F04: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule is highly suggestive of Primary Iris Lymphoma.
rationales.F05: The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement is highly suggestive of Primary Iris Lymphoma.
rationales.F07: The ciliary body involvement shown on ultrasonographic biomicroscopy is highly suggestive of Primary Iris Lymphoma.
rationales.F08: The presence of monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes is highly suggestive of lymphoma, particularly Primary Iris Lymphoma and Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
rationales.F10: The absence of systemic involvement makes Systemic Lymphoma with Ocular Involvement less likely.
